text:
The Kebarrow Compact’s twenty-year span from 2 to 21 was defined by internal instability and a cycle of retaliatory violence. The period began with a marriage binding the Compact to the Griwick Compact, but ended with Sou Dra still holding the seat after a failed challenge. Five people held the seat during this time, with the position passing four times. The Compact’s standing deteriorated significantly, marked by a rebellion in 15 that followed the outlawing of Witrou Breim.

Searn Sisrill ruled until 8, when Math Ham killed him at Kebarrow. Reweld Wul took the seat by election and served for six years. His rule ended when Witrou Breim had him murdered at Kebarrow in 14. Witrou Breim then took the seat by election. He faced an open challenge from Pouldrir Ho in 15, losing the seat and being cast out. Pouldrir Ho ruled for five years until Turaer Danpa had him murdered at Kebarrow in 20. Sou Dra took the seat by election in 20 and held it through 21, surviving an open challenge from Thra Bround that year.

The Compact engaged in eight raids, three of which carried off plunder, two got through but took nothing, and three were beaten off. It suffered six raids, all by the Griwick Compact or the Wurn League. Four of its own people were murdered from within. Two were cast out, and one was declared outlaw. Four exiles returned to serve the Compact. Hunger at Meigate in 10 killed 23 people. Meigate rose against the Compact in 15, when its standing had fallen very low. Four people were courted away from its ruler.

The Griwick Compact’s twenty-year span from 24 to 43 was defined by violent succession, relentless warfare, and a steady erosion of its territorial integrity. The period opened with a coup that installed Bu Rumpirn, who was swiftly overthrown by Thold Valmaer, establishing a pattern of unstable rule where eight individuals held the seat in rapid succession. Griwick fought six battles, winning all of them, yet it lost two places and suffered a plague that killed 640 people. By the end, the Compact had destroyed two rival powers, the Wurn League and the Kebarrow Compact, but its own standing had collapsed, leading to internal murders and the casting out of its rulers.

Thold Valmaer and Bu Rumpirn exchanged the seat through coups in 24, with Valmaer ultimately killing Rumpirn’s successor, Nael War, in 34. Nael War then ruled until he was killed by Stonand Ker in 34. Kondruth Tru took the seat in 37 after killing Nael War, but was himself killed by Beas Krouthea in 37. Durnrin Drar succeeded him in 37, only to be murdered by Stonand Ker in 41. Heth Fal took the seat in 41 by setting aside the claim of Sor Pean, but was cast out in 42 after losing an open challenge to Throll Kell. Throll Kell held the seat at the end of the period. Four rulers were killed, three were cast out, and one remained in power.

Griwick sent three raids, all successful: against Hadale in 24, Kebarrow in 26, and Vea Lode in 42. It suffered fourteen raids, six of which carried off plunder. It fought six battles, all victories: twice against the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode, twice against the Wurn League at Hadale, and twice against the Kebarrow Compact at Kebarrow. It began three wars, spending six years at war. It took Hadale from the Wurn League in 34 and Kebarrow from the Kebarrow Compact in 39. It lost Vea Lode to the Vea Lode Covenant in 29. Two places, Threi Cut and Laehiford, rose against it when its standing had fallen to nothing. A plague killed 640 people across five years of sickness. One marriage tied it to the Wurn League in 29.

The Wurn League’s twenty-year span, from year 2 to 21, was defined by a rapid expansion of alliances followed by a catastrophic military collapse against the Griwick Compact. The period began with the League securing Threi Cut and binding itself to both major neighboring powers through six marriages. It ended with the League having lost two strategic places, its ruler killed, and its military reputation shattered by four consecutive defeats. The Griwick Compact emerged as the dominant force, while the Kebarrow Compact remained a distant, raiding neighbor.

At the start, the League consolidated its position by occupying Threi Cut in year 2 and weaving a dense network of ties to the Kebarrow Compact and the Griwick Compact through six marriages between years 3 and 20. This diplomatic activity masked a growing vulnerability. In year 5, the Griwick Compact declared war on the League over Threi Cut. The League initially won a battle at Threi Cut in year 5, killing 45 Griwickians, but the conflict quickly turned. The Griwick Compact defeated the League at Threi Cut in year 6 (35 dead) and again at Threi Cut in year 7 (29 dead), taking Threi Cut from the League in that same year. The League’s fortunes worsened as it lost Laehiford to the Griwick Compact in year 8 after a defeat there (107 dead) and lost Hadale in year 9 after another defeat (101 dead).

Internal instability accompanied these external losses. Reweld Wul was cast out in year 7 for attempted murder, allowing Math Ham to take the seat by setting aside the named heir Witrou Breim. Math Ham’s rule was brief and violent; he ordered the murder of Searn Sisrill at Kebarrow in year 8 and was himself killed by Kei Leassel at Hadale in year 10. Trem Lolkoll took the seat by right of birth in year 10 and held it until the end of the period. The League’s military capacity had eroded significantly; of the seven raids it sent out, four were beaten off and two took nothing, with only one carrying off plunder. The period ended with Trem Lolkoll still holding the seat, but the League had lost two places and fought five battles, winning only one.

The Kebarrow Compact’s nineteen-year tenure from 22 to 40 was defined by a relentless war with the Griwick Compact and a succession of internal purges that left its leadership fractured. The period began with Sou Dra holding the seat, a position he maintained through open challenges and the execution of conspirators, but ended with the Compact finished, its land lost and its followers scattered. Five people held the seat during this time, each ruling for an average of 3.4 years, with the seat passing four times. The Compact fought four battles, all lost to the Griwick Compact, and suffered two major defeats at Kebarrow that directly precipitated its destruction.

Sou Dra’s rule was marked by violent consolidation and external aggression. He survived a conspiracy by Turaer Danpa in 25, leading to Danpa’s execution, and later ordered the murder of Thold Valmaer at Griwick in 28. His authority was challenged openly by Tor Nathgoull in 29; Sou Dra lost the seat and was cast out. Tor Nathgoull then took the seat by coup after winning a challenge in 32, but his rule was short-lived. He was cast out in 35 after losing an open challenge to Beas Krouthea. Beas Krouthea’s tenure ended in 38 when he was murdered by Kou Peis at Kebarrow, an act of internal violence that left the seat vacant until Diweith Mound took it by election later that year.

The external conflict with the Griwick Compact escalated throughout the period. The Kebarrow Compact sent four raids, two of which were beaten off, one that took nothing, and one that carried off plunder. In retaliation, the Griwick Compact raided Kebarrow in 26, carrying off grain. The two powers fought four battles, all lost by the Kebarrow Compact: at Vea Lode in 27 and 28, and at Kebarrow in 38 and 39. The defeat at Kebarrow in 39 resulted in the Griwick Compact taking the settlement from the Kebarrow Compact. In the same year, the Kebarrow Compact was finished, its last nine followers scattering. The period ended with the Griwick Compact making peace after the collapse of its rival.

The Wurn League’s fourteen-year span from 22 to 35 was defined by internal fragmentation and external defeat. The period began with Trem Lolkoll holding the seat, but his rule was immediately undermined by conspiracy. Befu Seirn’s plot against him was uncovered in 22, leading to Seirn’s execution. This instability marked the start of a rapid succession of rulers, with the seat passing eight times among nine individuals. The League’s authority eroded through a series of violent takeovers and purges, culminating in its destruction by the Griwick Compact.

Internal strife drove the early years. Nael War’s conspiracy against Trem Lolkoll was uncovered in 25, resulting in War’s exile. In 26, Gatros Hearn challenged and defeated Trem Lolkoll, taking the seat by coup. Sothkel Sald then challenged Hearn, winning and taking the seat by coup, before killing Hearn at Hadale. Sald himself was challenged by Saern Meastouth, who took the seat by coup and killed Sald at Hadale. Saern’s rule ended in 27 when his attempt on Thold Valmaer failed, leading to his exile. Teapeall Heampim took the seat by right of birth, ruling until his death in 28. Paernrom Sir contested the claim of the named heir Bu Rumpirn, winning by primogeniture and taking the seat, while Bu Rumpirn was cast out. Paernrom Sir was murdered by Stonand Ker in 30, and Heillvar Maer took the seat by right of birth. Heillvar’s rule ended in 32 after his attempt on Nael War failed, leading to his exile. Drarka Draernthun took the seat by right of birth.

The League’s external conflicts mirrored its internal decay. It suffered one raid by the Griwick Compact in 24, which carried off plunder from Hadale. Three raids sent by the League against the Griwick Compact in 29 and 31 were all beaten off. In 33, the Griwick Compact declared war on the Wurn League. Stonand Ker challenged and defeated Drarka Draernthun, taking the seat by coup. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in 33, killing 58, and again in 34, killing 87. In 34, the Griwick Compact took Hadale from the Wurn League. The Wurn League was finished, its last 25 followers scattering. Peace was made between the Griwick Compact and the Wurn League in 35, after the League’s collapse.

The Vea Lode Covenant began in year 29 when Vea Lode broke from the Griwick Compact, with Mothgall Vafarn taking the seat. The new power immediately faced a famine that killed 11 people and left grain short. The crisis deepened in the following years, with 13 more dying and 32 abandoning the place in year 31, followed by 9 deaths and 22 departures in year 32, and 7 deaths with 30 leaving in year 33. The internal stability of the Covenant collapsed in year 33 when Sou Dra had Mothgall Vafarn murdered at Vea Lode. Sou Dra then took the seat by election.

Bu Rumpirn and Sou Dra both returned from exile to serve the Covenant in year 30. After Sou Dra secured the seat, the Covenant turned outward, raiding Griwick in year 34 and carrying off 36 grain and killing 20. In year 35, the Covenant raided Laehiford, taking 44 grain and killing 28. The internal violence resumed in year 36 when Bu Rumpirn had Sou Dra murdered at Vea Lode. Bu Rumpirn took the seat by election following Sou Dra’s death.

Bu Rumpirn ruled until his death in year 39 at the age of 60. With his death, the Vea Lode Covenant came to an end, and its one place fell to no one. The period saw three rulers: Mothgall Vafarn, Sou Dra, and Bu Rumpirn. Two of these rulers were killed. The Covenant’s existence was marked by famine, murder, and raids, ending with its dissolution.

The Griwick Compact’s twenty-year span from year 4 to 23 was defined by a violent struggle for territory against the Wurn League and internal instability that eroded its authority. The period began with the Compact exploiting a famine at Vea Lode to raid Kebarrow, but it ended with the seat held by Thold Valmaer after a succession decided by strength. Throughout the era, the Compact fought five battles against the Wurn League, winning four and losing one. It sent six raids, all of which carried off plunder, while suffering ten raids, six of which were beaten off. The power’s standing deteriorated from very low to nothing, prompting two places to rise against it, and its leadership changed hands three times through death, exile, and murder.

In year 4, the Compact raided Kebarrow, killing 28 and taking 43 grain, a direct response to the famine at Vea Lode. The following year, it declared war on the Wurn League for Threi Cut. The conflict opened with a defeat at Threi Cut in year 5, where 45 of the Compact’s forces died. By year 6, Pouldrir Ho had married Kirn Dae, binding the Compact to the Kebarrow Compact. The Compact reversed its military fortunes in year 6 by defeating the Wurn League at Threi Cut, and again in year 7 at the same site. In year 7, it took Threi Cut from the Wurn League, and in year 8, it took Laehiford after defeating the Wurn League there. The war ended in year 10 after five years of fighting. During this time, the Compact raided Laehiford, Hadale, and Meigate, carrying off grain and killing hundreds.

Internal cohesion fractured in year 9 when Pouldrir Ho was cast out for an attempted murder. Kei Leassel took the seat by defeating the named heir Turaer Danpa in a contest decided by strength. Vea Lode rose against the Compact that same year as its standing fell very low. Kei Leassel ruled until his death in year 17. Witrou Breim took the seat after rejecting Beirn Naem’s claim. Witrou Breim was murdered in year 23 by Bu Rumpirn. Thold Valmaer took the seat by the strongest claim. The Compact’s authority had fallen to nothing by year 12, when Threi Cut rose against it. The period ended with Thold Valmaer holding the seat.

The Meigate Covenant began in 29 as a breakaway from the Kebarrow Compact, with Raes Go taking the seat. Its early years were defined by failed aggression and internal consolidation. Raes Go married Mothgall Vafarn in 30, binding the Covenant to the Vea Lode Covenant. Raids on Griwick in 31 and Laehiford in 33 were both beaten off. The ruler’s position was challenged openly in 43 by Heillvar Maer, who lost and was cast out. Raes Go himself was cast out in 44 after losing an open challenge to Diweith Mound. Diweith Mound ruled until he was killed in 46, at which point Drarka Draernthun took the seat by setting aside the claim of the named heir Tor Nathgoull.

The period saw two wars with the Griwick Compact, one of which lasted two years. The Covenant declared war in 47 over a long-standing grievance. It raided Griwick in 47, carrying off 23 grain and killing 16, but was defeated at Threi Cut later that year with 12 dead. It was defeated again at Threi Cut in 48 with 10 dead. Peace was made in 49. The Covenant suffered raids from the Griwick Compact in 42 and 45. It sent eight raids in total; four were beaten off, and four carried off plunder. Three marriages tied the Covenant to other powers: the Vea Lode Covenant in 30, and the Griwick Compact in 35 and 50.

The Covenant’s standing fell to nothing in 45 when Vea Lode rose against it. Hunger killed 68 people across the period, with 61 dying at Meigate in 38. Eleven exiles returned to service. Three people were courted away from its ruler. The period ended in 51 with Drarka Draernthun still holding the seat. The seat passed from one person to another two times inside this period. Two battles were fought, both lost. One war was begun. One place was taken.

The Griwick Compact endured eight years of violent internal turnover and external war, defined by a succession of six rulers who held the seat for an average of 1.1 years each. The period began with the murder of Throll Kell by Lorn Waldhith at Griwick in 44, a act that allowed Tum Ga to seize the seat by the strongest claim. Tum Ga’s rule lasted only until Stonand Ker challenged and won in 45, taking the seat by coup and casting Tum Ga out. The Compact’s internal stability remained fragile; Lorn Waldhith was cast out in 45 for a conspiracy uncovered after two years, and Stonand Ker was murdered by Kou Peis at Hadale in 47.

Kou Peis’s brief tenure ended when Thres Thrild, the named heir, had his claim upheld against Drouldthas Stour in 47, taking the seat while Drouldthas was cast out. Thres Thrild’s rule was marked by war with the Meigate Covenant, which declared war in 47. The Compact fought two battles at Threi Cut, winning both in 47 and 48, with 12 and 10 dead respectively. Despite these victories, the Compact suffered raids on Griwick in 47 and Hadale in 51, and a raid on Laehiford in 49 was beaten off. Peace was made in 49 after two years of conflict.

Internal purges continued as Kou Peis was executed for conspiracy in 48. Raes Go took the seat by coup in 49 after challenging Thres Thrild, who was cast out. Raes Go was killed by Paernmel Has in 50, who then took the seat. The period ended with Paernmel Has still holding the seat in 51. Throughout the eight years, four people were killed, two cast out, and four cast out for losing claims or conspiracies. Three exiles returned to service. The Compact sent one raid on Meigate in 45, which took nothing. Eleven people were courted away from its ruler, signaling a house coming apart. The quarrel with the Meigate Covenant persisted through two battles.

Drarka Draernthun took the seat of the Meigate Covenant in 46 after contesting the claim of the named heir Tor Nathgoull in an election. The previous ruler, Diweith Mound, had been killed by Stonand Ker at Meigate earlier that year. Drarka’s victory set aside Tor’s claim, and Tor was cast out. The period began with the Meigate Covenant holding the seat, a position Drarka retained until the end of the years in 51. One person had held the seat during this time, and the other, Diweith, had been killed.

The Meigate Covenant declared war on the Griwick Compact in 47 over a long-standing grievance. The Covenant raided Griwick, carrying off 23 grain and killing 16, but was defeated by the Griwick Compact at Threi Cut later that year, with 12 dead. A second defeat followed at Threi Cut in 48, with 10 dead. The war lasted 2 years, ending in peace in 49 when both sides were exhausted. During the period, the Meigate Covenant sent out three raids: one against Griwick in 47 that carried off plunder, one against Laehiford in 49 that was beaten off, and one against Hadale in 51 that carried off 49 grain and killed 14. No battles were won.

Five exiles returned to take service with the Meigate Covenant: Lorn Waldhith in 47, Tum Ga in 48, Drouldthas Stour in 49, Heth Fal in 50, and Thres Thrild in 50. Lorn Waldhith died in 49. A marriage in 50 between Hehum Skul and Ta Poveil bound the Meigate Covenant to the Griwick Compact. Hunger at Vea Lode lasted 3 years, killing 2 people in total. Drarka Draernthun won Kaes Rou away from the previous ruler in 46. The period ended in 51 with Drarka Draernthun still holding the seat.

In year 50, Paernmel Has challenged Raes Go openly for the Griwick Compact and won the seat. He killed Raes Go at Griwick later that same year. Tor Nathgoull was raised to steward of the Griwick Compact in year 50.

In year 51, Visal Veill married Treild Haen at Hadale. Paernmel Has’s child, Gim Raeldrol, was born at Kebarrow. Voudreirn Wer, Trurkeand Busi, and Ta Poveil each won Bakrei Dea away from the ruler of the Griwick Compact. The Griwick Compact spent 205 silver buying goodwill for the fifth time and was not believed. The Meigate Covenant raided Hadale, carrying off 49 grain and killing 14.

The Griwick Compact declared war on the Wurn League in year 5 for Threi Cut. The Wurn League defeated the Griwick Compact at Threi Cut in year 5, with 45 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Threi Cut in year 6, with 35 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Threi Cut in year 7, with 29 dead. The Griwick Compact took Threi Cut from the Wurn League in year 7.

The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Laehiford in year 8, with 107 dead. The Griwick Compact took Laehiford from the Wurn League in year 8. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in year 9, with 101 dead. The Griwick Compact and the Wurn League made peace after 5 years in year 10, both sides exhausted.

The war began in 27 when the Kebarrow Compact declared it on the Griwick Compact over a long-standing grievance. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode in the same year, with 57 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode again in 28, with 48 dead.

In 28, Sou Dra had Thold Valmaer murdered at Griwick. The conflict continued until 29, when the Kebarrow Compact and the Griwick Compact made peace after two years, both sides exhausted.
